propositions: Pure-agentic single-pass completion verification produces false-positive rejections when AC prose does not align perfectly with available evidence; a hybrid filter+fallback approach aims to eliminate false-positive rejections by construction

A deterministic single-pass FILTER that can only PASS or ABSTAIN (never REJECT) per criterion, followed by narrowed agentic verification of abstained ACs, achieves -26% token cost overall and -46% on all-met corpus with zero false passes on adversarial unmet ACs

The completion verifier enforces an 8000-character description admission cap that rejects tickets or reduced-ticket-text over that limit; adversarial corpus modifications must be length-neutral to avoid deterministic fast-fails

Filter PASS/ABSTAIN judgments depend on AC style and surrounding ticket context: ACs naming greppable artifacts (tests, symbols, files) can PASS from static evidence packs; ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts rationally ABSTAIN, yielding bimodal coverage (0-90% per ticket)

The criteria-reduction seam in verify_completion via monkeypatching rebar._reads.show_ticket successfully narrows the AC block for fallback runs and auto-narrows the step budget, enabling clean integration of filter outputs including multi-child epic traversal

Agentic verifier variance (±30% single-run deltas, low-rate false-FAILs on genuinely-met ACs) dominates cost comparisons on identical criteria sets; filter cost is negligible (~0.4% of control agentic spend) so the design is cost-neutral worst-case and 60-80% better on test-citing AC styles
